Only shown when provided (edit mode). Create a copy of the node in your state.

props.name: onAddNode
props.description:
Called in edit mode when the user clicks empty canvas space (no pan occurred).
Receives the click position in canvas coordinates (center of the new node).
Add a new node at that position in your state.

props.name: onAddEdge
props.description:
Called in edit mode when the user draws a connector between two nodes using
the connect button on a node. Add the new edge in your state.

props.name: nodeMenuItems
props.type: (nodeId: string) => Array<{ id: string; label?: string; icon?: string; variant?: string; disabled?: boolean; onClick?: () => void } | { type: 'divider'; id: string } | { type: 'group'; id: string; label: string }>
props.description:
Returns custom context menu items for a right-clicked node.
Items use the `ContextMenuEntry` shape from the A1 ContextMenu component.
Shown before the built-in "Duplicate" and "Delete" items (edit mode only).

props.name: canvasMenuItems
props.type: Array<{ id: string; label?: string; icon?: string; variant?: string; disabled?: boolean; onClick?: () => void } | { type: 'divider'; id: string }>
props.description:
Extra context menu items shown when right-clicking the canvas background
(appended below the built-in zoom / fit / reset items).

props.name: showGrid
props.description: Show the visual grid (default `true`)

props.name: gridType
props.description:
Visual grid pattern (default `"lines"`).
- `"lines"` — horizontal and vertical rules every `gridSpacing` pixels.
- `"dots"` — one dot every `gridSpacing` pixels in both directions.

props.name: background
props.description:
Background surface token (default `"panel"`).
- `"panel"` — standard panel surface.
- `"page"` — page background.
- `"raised"` — elevated surface.
Pair with `inverse` for a dark/inverse canvas.

props.name: inverse
props.description:
Apply the inverse color scheme — dark surface with inverse text.
Mirrors the `inverse` prop on `Section`. Default `false`.

props.name: showControls
props.description: Show the zoom controls overlay (default `true`)

props.name: edgeStyle
props.description:
Default edge rendering shape for all edges (default `"straight"`).
Individual `<NodeConnector curved>` overrides this per connector.

props.name: defaultAnchorSnap
props.description:
Canvas-wide anchor snap default for all nodes.
Per-node `anchorSnap` overrides this when set.
- `'cardinal'`  — exits only from N, E, S, W face centers (90°)
- `'octagonal'` — exits from all 8 directions including diagonals (45°)
- `undefined`   — free angle toward the target (default)

Does not affect `edgeStyle="elbow"` edges.

props.name: snapToGrid
props.description:
When `true`, node positions snap to the nearest grid increment
while dragging in `mode="edit"` (default `false`).

props.name: gridSpacing
props.description:
Grid cell size in pixels (default `16`). Applies to the visual grid overlay
and to snap-to-grid when `snapToGrid` is enabled.
Suggested values: `1`, `4`, `8`, `16`.

props.name: defaultZoom
props.description: Initial zoom level (default `1`)

props.name: defaultPan
props.description: Initial pan offset in pixels (default `{ x: 0, y: 0 }`)

props.name: traceConnections
props.description:
When `true`, clicking an already-selected node toggles a transitive
connection trace — all connectors reachable from that node are highlighted
and the rest are dimmed. Click the node again to dismiss. Default `false`.

props.name: draggableNodes
props.description:
When `true`, nodes are draggable (grab cursor, position updates via `onNodeMove`)
without enabling full `mode="edit"` (no connect buttons, no double-click-to-add).
Ignored when `mode="edit"` (edit mode always implies draggable). Default `false`.

props.name: highlightConnections
props.description:
When `true` and a node is selected, connectors directly attached to that node
are highlighted and all others are dimmed. Ignored when `traceConnections` is
active. Default `false`.

props.name: onSelectionChange
props.description:
Called when the selected node changes. Fires with the node id when a node
is selected, or `null` when the selection is cleared.

props.name: onEdgeSelect
props.description:
Called when a connector is clicked. Fires with the connector id when selected,
or `null` when selection is cleared.

props.name: 'aria-label'
props.description: Accessible label for the canvas region (required)

highlights:
> **Compositional API — `Node` and `CanvasEdge` as children:**
>
> ```jsx
> <Canvas aria-label="Graph">
>   <Node id="a" x={100} y={100} label="Tokens" color="info" />
>   <Node id="b" x={300} y={100} label="React" color="success" />
>   <CanvasEdge id="e1" from="a" to="b" />
> </Canvas>
> ```
>
> **Canvas props:** `mode` (`"view"` default | `"edit"` — in edit mode nodes are draggable), `onNodeMove` (`(id, x, y) => void` — called when a node is dragged in edit mode), `onDeleteNode(id)` — called when "Delete" is chosen from a node's context menu (only shown in `edit` mode), `nodeMenuItems(id)` — returns `ContextMenuEntry[]` of custom items for a right-clicked node (shown before Delete), `canvasMenuItems` — extra items appended to the canvas right-click menu (below the built-in zoom/fit/reset items), `showGrid` (boolean, default true — dot grid overlay), `background` (`"panel"` default | `"page"` | `"raised"`), `inverse` (boolean, default false — applies the inverse surface and text color, mirroring Section's inverse prop; combine with any `background`), `showControls` (boolean, default true — zoom controls overlay), `edgeStyle` (`"straight"` default | `"curved"` — quadratic Bézier connectors; a per-edge `curved` boolean on `CanvasEdge` overrides this), `snapToGrid` (boolean, default false — rounds dragged node positions to 24px grid increments in edit mode), `defaultZoom` (number, default 1), `defaultPan` (`{ x, y }`, default `{ x: 0, y: 0 }`), `aria-label` (string, required). Pan: left-click drag, middle-click drag, or single-finger touch drag. Zoom: wheel toward cursor, or two-finger pinch. Controls: zoom in/out/fit-all/reset. Right-click canvas background → built-in zoom context menu. Right-click node → custom + delete items.
>
> **Node props:** `label` (required), `id?`, `x?`, `y?` (canvas-space px, center of node — needed when used inside Canvas for positioning and edge routing), `sublabel?`, `shape?` (`circle` default), `color?` (`neutral` default), `subtle?` (boolean). Standalone: renders inline at natural dimensions with no Canvas context needed. Inside Canvas: absolutely positioned; selection, drag, and context-menu callbacks are injected from `CanvasCtx`.
>
> **Accessibility:** In view mode, a node is a focusable button with pressed
> state for selection. In edit mode, where the node contains a separate
> connection button, the outer node uses non-focusable group semantics so
> interactive controls are not nested and cannot intercept the connection
> button's native keyboard activation. Node labels provide the accessible names,
> and status foreground/background pairs are token governed.
>
> **Node shapes:** `circle` (default, 80×80px) · `square` (80×80px, `--base-radius-md`) · `squircle` (80×80px, `--base-radius-xl`) · `rectangle` (128×56px). Edge routing correctly intersects circle circumference or rectangle boundary.
>
> **Node colors:** `neutral / info / success / warn / error / accent`. Add `subtle` for a tinted surface (uses `*-surface` tokens) instead of the full status background.
>
> **CanvasEdge props:** `id` (required), `from`, `to` (CanvasNode ids), `direction` (`"to"` default | `"from"` | `"both"` | `"none"`), `variant` (`"solid"` default | `"dashed"` | `"dotted"`), `weight` (`"normal"` default | `"heavy"`), `label?` (rendered at the midpoint), `curved?` (boolean — overrides the canvas-level `edgeStyle` for this specific edge). CanvasEdge is a descriptor: returns null and Canvas draws the SVG connector.
>
> **Status:** Experimental — React only. Node size is driven by `component.canvas.node.size` token (80px). Arrowhead markers use stable per-canvas-instance IDs (React `useId`) so multiple Canvas instances on the same page don't collide.

components.name: Node

props.name: id
props.description:
Unique identifier — required when used inside `<Canvas>` so edges can reference it.
Optional when used standalone.

props.name: x
props.description: Center X position in canvas space (pixels) — used by Canvas for positioning.

props.name: y
props.description: Center Y position in canvas space (pixels) — used by Canvas for positioning.

props.name: label
props.description: Primary label displayed inside the node

props.name: sublabel
props.description: Optional secondary label shown below the main label

props.name: title
props.description: Native tooltip shown on hover — use for full token names or supplementary context

props.name: shape
props.description:
Node shape. `circle` (default) and `square` / `squircle` are square.
`rectangle` is wider than it is tall.

props.name: color
props.description: Color variant (default `"neutral"`)

props.name: size
props.description:
T-shirt size (default `"md"`). Scales both the node dimensions and the label font size.
- `xs` — 40px / 80×36px rect
- `sm` — 60px / 96×44px rect
- `md` — 80px / 128×56px rect (default)
- `lg` — 120px / 160×72px rect
- `xl` — 160px / 200×88px rect

props.name: subtle
props.description: When true, uses a tinted surface instead of the full status background (default `false`)

props.name: backgroundColor
props.description:
Custom background color for the node (any valid CSS color: hex, rgb, hsl, `var(--token)`).
When set, overrides the `color` / `subtle` token-based background and border color.
Use `foregroundColor` alongside it if the default text color doesn't have enough contrast.

props.name: foregroundColor
props.description:
Custom text (foreground) color. Only meaningful when `backgroundColor` is also set.
Accepts any valid CSS color value.

props.name: anchorSnap
props.description:
Constrains where connectors may exit/enter this node.
Overrides the Canvas-level `defaultAnchorSnap` when set.
- `'cardinal'`  — only N, E, S, W (90° increments)
- `'octagonal'` — N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW (45° increments)
- `undefined`   — inherits Canvas `defaultAnchorSnap` or uses free angle (default)

Does not affect `edgeStyle="elbow"` edges, which always use cardinal exits.

rules.requirement: Do not place interactive descendants inside an ActionTiles item when that tile item is itself interactive.
rules.do: Use a non-interactive ActionTiles item when it contains switches, buttons, menus, links, or other controls. Reserve clickable tile items for a single destination or command.
rules.dont: Render the whole tile as a button or link and also place nested controls inside it.

rules.requirement: An interactive ActionTiles item should represent one clear primary action or destination.
rules.do: Keep the title, subtitle, icon, and supporting slots aligned around one action such as opening settings, jumping to a workflow, or toggling a focused preference.
rules.dont: Mix unrelated actions in one tile or use the tile chrome as a generic content card.

rules.requirement: The BottomDrawer accepts a maximum of 5 items. Exceeding this limit crowds the bar and makes touch targets too narrow. The component silently truncates to 5.
Every item must have a Material Symbols icon name. The icon is the primary visual identifier on a small screen; a label-only item is not permitted.
Every item must have a short text label (1–2 words). Icon-only navigation is inaccessible — labels provide context for low-vision and cognitive accessibility.

When used with TopHeader, set navIconPosition={{ xs: "hidden", sm: "above" }} (or similar breakpoint object) on TopHeader so the hamburger and nav are suppressed at xs. The BottomDrawer then provides the sole navigation at xs. Use a CSS media query (min-width: 481px) to hide the BottomDrawer at sm+.
The BottomDrawer applies env(safe-area-inset-bottom) padding to avoid overlap with iOS home indicator. Do not add additional bottom padding on top of this.
Use clear, action-oriented labels that describe what will happen.
rules.do: Use labels like "Save changes", "Create account", "Download report", or "Cancel order".
rules.dont: Use vague labels like "Submit", "OK", "Yes", or "Continue" when the action is not obvious.

rules.requirement: Use button hierarchy to communicate action priority.
rules.do: Use primary, secondary, tertiary, destructive, and icon button variants consistently.
rules.dont: Give multiple unrelated actions the same visual weight.

rules.requirement: Use only one primary button within a single decision area.
rules.do: Make the main recommended action the only primary button in a form, dialog, or action group.
rules.dont: Place several primary buttons together and force users to compare competing actions.

rules.requirement: Do not rely on color alone to communicate purpose, priority, or risk.
rules.do: Pair visual treatment with clear labels, icons, helper text, or confirmation patterns when needed.
rules.dont: Use only red, green, or another color to indicate meaning.

rules.requirement: Make destructive actions explicit and harder to trigger accidentally.
rules.do: Use labels like "Delete project" or "Remove member" and add confirmation for high-risk actions.
rules.dont: Use vague labels like "Confirm" for destructive actions.

rules.requirement: Match button emphasis to the importance and risk of the action.
rules.do: Make the primary action visually strongest and keep secondary actions quieter.
rules.dont: Make destructive or low-priority actions look like the preferred next step unless context requires it.

rules.requirement: Keep button labels short, specific, and scannable.
rules.do: Use concise labels, usually two to four words.
rules.dont: Use long sentence-style labels unless necessary for clarity.

rules.requirement: Use verbs for action buttons.
rules.do: Use labels like "Edit profile", "Add payment method", or "Download invoice".
rules.dont: Use noun-only labels like "Profile", "Payment method", or "Invoice" for actions.

rules.requirement: Tertiary buttons must always include both a visible icon and a verb-led label.
rules.do: Pair every button with a relevant icon and a verb label so users can identify the action visually and by meaning.
rules.dont: Use a button with text only or an icon only — an icon adds scannability, and the verb ensures the action is understood without relying on shape alone.

rules.requirement: Place actions consistently across similar interfaces.
rules.do: Keep primary, secondary, cancel, and destructive actions in predictable positions.
rules.dont: Move equivalent actions to different locations across similar screens or dialogs.

rules.requirement: Button alignment should match the alignment of the surrounding content.
rules.do: Align buttons with the content they act on.
rules.dont: Center or right-align buttons when the related content is left-aligned.

rules.requirement: Only center buttons when the parent content is also centered.
rules.do: Center buttons in empty states, confirmations, or other centered layouts.
rules.dont: Center buttons under left-aligned headings, body copy, forms, or settings.

rules.requirement: Right-aligned buttons should only be used when the parent area is clearly defined and does not create a floating button effect.
rules.do: Right-align buttons inside a clear parent container such as a dialog footer, card, or panel.
rules.dont: Place a right-aligned button in open space where it appears detached from the content it affects.

rules.requirement: Provide a large enough clickable or tappable target.
rules.do: Use a minimum target size of 44 by 44 pixels for touch interactions.
rules.dont: Make buttons or icon buttons difficult to click, tap, or focus.

rules.requirement: Define clear visual states for all button interactions.
rules.do: Provide default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, success, and error states as needed.
rules.dont: Leave buttons without visible focus, loading, or disabled states.

rules.requirement: Provide a clearly visible focus state for keyboard users.
rules.do: Use a focus indicator that is easy to see and distinct from hover or active states.
rules.dont: Remove focus outlines without replacing them with an accessible alternative.

rules.requirement: Explain why a button is disabled when the reason is not obvious.
rules.do: Provide helper text, validation messages, or visible requirements near the button or related fields.
rules.dont: Disable a button with no explanation and leave users guessing what to fix.

rules.requirement: Use loading states to prevent duplicate actions.
rules.do: Show progress with labels like "Saving..." and prevent repeat submissions while the action is processing.
rules.dont: Allow users to click the same action repeatedly while a request is in progress.

rules.requirement: Icon-only buttons must have accessible names.
rules.do: Provide an aria-label, tooltip when useful, and a large enough hit area.
rules.dont: Rely on the icon alone to communicate the action to all users.

rules.requirement: Use buttons for actions and links for navigation.
rules.do: Use a button for saving, submitting, deleting, opening a modal, or changing state.
rules.dont: Use buttons for basic navigation when a link would be semantically correct.

rules.requirement: Icon buttons are always a fixed, square, natural-width control and must never be stretched to fill their container.
rules.do: Let the icon button size itself from its size token (md or lg). When you need a full-width action, use a Button with fullWidth and a text label instead.
rules.dont: Apply fullWidth, width:100%, flex:1, or any other stretching to an IconButton, or wrap it in a layout that forces it to span the available width.

rules.requirement: Use the fullWidth prop only when a button should intentionally span its container.
rules.do: Use fullWidth for primary actions in narrow or mobile-width containers, stacked call-to-action groups, and form footers. Leave it off (natural width) everywhere else.
rules.dont: Stretch buttons to full width in wide layouts where a natural-width button reads better, and never apply fullWidth to an IconButton.

rules.requirement: Use the loading prop while an action is in progress so the button is inert and clearly communicates that work is happening.
rules.do: Set loading during async work such as form submission; pair it with a present-tense label like "Saving…" and rely on the built-in spinner and aria-busy state.
rules.dont: Leave a button interactive during a long-running action, or hand-roll a separate spinner when the loading prop already provides one.

rules.requirement: Keep the button system limited to reusable, purposeful variants.
rules.do: Provide a standard set such as primary, secondary, tertiary, destructive, text, and icon buttons.
rules.dont: Create one-off button styles for individual screens or edge cases.

rules.requirement: Node dimensions must come from component tokens, not hardcoded values.
Do not place a Canvas inside another Canvas.
When mode="edit", provide an onNodesChange callback to persist dragged positions.
Always provide an aria-label on Canvas describing the graph's purpose.
Do not place interactive elements inside a Card when the Card itself is the interactive element.
rules.do: Use `variant="navigation"` with a single `href` or navigation handler, and keep the card contents to static text, icons, images, lists, and layout components.
rules.dont: Put buttons, links, form controls, menus, tabs, or other clickable controls inside a navigation Card.

rules.requirement: Use navigation Cards only when the entire card represents one destination.
rules.do: Make the Card destination match the title and supporting content.
rules.dont: Use a navigation Card when different parts of the card imply different actions or destinations.

rules.requirement: Do not use Card to create page-level sections or large content blocks.
rules.do: Use `Section` for page-level regions — it provides the correct surface, padding, width constraints, and theme support. Reserve Card for small, repeated, bounded content units such as product tiles, user profiles, summary items, or navigation destinations.
rules.dont: Wrap a hero, a full-page form, a marketing row, an article body, or any other large block of content in a Card. A Card that spans a full content column or contains a long-form layout is a misuse of the component.

rules.requirement: A set of two or more sibling Cards (product tiles, feature cards, profiles) should be laid out in a Grid, not placed loosely in a Stack or Section.
rules.do: Wrap repeated Cards in `<Grid columns={{ xs: 1, md: 3 }} gap="md">` so they form even rows that reflow responsively.
rules.dont: Drop several Cards directly into a Section or Stack where they stretch full-width or wrap unevenly.

rules.requirement: An image inside a Card should declare a valid, consistent aspect ratio so a grid of cards has uniform image heights.
rules.do: Set `aspectRatio` on the card's `Figure` to a token value (`16:9`, `4:3`, `3:2`, `1:1`, `2:3`, `3:4`, `9:16`, `21:9`) and use the same ratio across all cards in the same grid.
rules.dont: Omit `aspectRatio` (images render at varying natural heights) or pass a CSS-style value like `"4 / 3"` — only the colon token values apply a ratio.

rules.requirement: A Card's `status` must be conveyed by text, not by the colour stripe alone. Colour-only status fails WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.1 Use of Color (Level A). If the status is shown only by colour, it is not WCAG compliant.
rules.do: Whenever you set `status`, also display the status as text — pass `statusLabel` so the stripe is paired with a text badge, or make sure the status is named in visible text the card carries or sits within (a status badge in the card content, or a labelled column/lane the card belongs to, e.g. a Kanban board grouped by status). Treat the stripe and the `statusPulse` animation as decorative reinforcement of that text.
rules.dont: Set `status` with no `statusLabel` and no other visible status text, so the colour stripe (or the pulse animation) is the only way to tell one status from another. Never rely on colour or motion alone to communicate status.

rules.requirement: Use the A1 Recharts wrappers for chart surfaces.
rules.do: Render data visualizations through the named A1 chart wrapper that matches the visualization type so axes, polar grids, legends, tooltips, focus, and series colors stay tokenized.
rules.dont: Import Recharts directly in product UI when the required visualization can be represented by an A1 chart component.

rules.requirement: Every chart needs a clear title or accessible name.
rules.do: Provide `title` for visible context, or pass `aria-label` when the surrounding heading already names the chart.
rules.dont: Ship an unlabeled chart that screen-reader users cannot identify.

rules.requirement: Series colors must be paired with text labels.
rules.do: Keep the legend or tooltip enabled, use clear series labels, and provide surrounding text for any critical takeaway.
rules.dont: Rely on color alone to communicate which series is meaningful, successful, risky, or failing.

rules.requirement: Use the built-in tokenized series tones.
rules.do: Choose `tone` values from accent, info, success, warn, error, and neutral when defining series or categorical data items.
rules.dont: Pass arbitrary hex, rgb, hsl, or brand colors directly to Recharts series, cells, nodes, or links in A1 UI.

rules.requirement: Chip labels should be short enough to scan in a wrapped row.
Selectable chips must be rendered inside a ChipGroup with a declared selection mode.
Navigation chips must use anchor semantics.
Filter chips that open a menu must expose menu trigger state.
Chip rows should explicitly decide whether they wrap.
Use DefinitionList for label/value pairs where the label names, qualifies, or identifies the value.
rules.do: Use DefinitionList for metadata, settings summaries, object details, contact details, record attributes, and compact stats where each value needs an explicit label.
rules.dont: Use DefinitionList for tabular comparison across many columns, free-form prose, navigation menus, or form inputs.

rules.requirement: Use `direction="column"` when values need more vertical reading room.
rules.do: Choose column layout for narrow containers, mobile-first summaries, multi-line values, long labels, or values containing headings or rich React content.
rules.dont: Force row layout when labels or values wrap so frequently that scanning becomes harder than reading top-to-bottom.

rules.requirement: Use `direction="row"` with `labelWidth="auto"` when labels are short and natural label widths are acceptable.
rules.do: Choose auto label width for compact metadata where each pair can size itself, such as invoice number, status, or short account details.
rules.dont: Use auto label width when multiple rows need strong vertical alignment for fast comparison.

rules.requirement: Use `direction="row"` with `labelWidth="fixed"` when aligned values improve scanning.
rules.do: Choose fixed label width for record details, profile summaries, order metadata, or settings readouts where users compare values down the column.
rules.dont: Use fixed label width in very narrow spaces where labels consume too much of the row; switch to column layout instead.

rules.requirement: Show copy buttons only for exact values users reasonably need to reuse.
rules.do: Enable copy for IDs, emails, phone numbers, addresses, URLs, API keys, confirmation codes, and other exact text values.
rules.dont: Add copy buttons to every descriptive value, status label, or value rendered as complex interactive content.

rules.requirement: Use heading-styled values only when the value is the dominant datum in the group.
rules.do: Use `valueHeadingProps` for financial totals, KPI values, important account state, or hero metadata that should use Heading sizing while keeping `<dt>`/`<dd>` semantics.
rules.dont: Use large heading values for ordinary metadata where body text hierarchy is sufficient.

rules.requirement: Dialog content must scroll vertically only; dialogs must not expose horizontal scrolling.
rules.do: Let the shared Dialog body own vertical scrolling, and make wide child content responsive, wrapping, clipped, or internally overflow-managed by the child component.
rules.dont: Add horizontal scrolling to the Dialog body or rely on a child that forces the dialog wider than the viewport; fix the child layout or use that child's own governed overflow pattern instead.

rules.requirement: Always size badges to the natural width of their content.
rules.do: Let the badge hug its label and optional icon.
rules.dont: Stretch badges to fill a parent container, grid column, or full row.

rules.requirement: Keep badge labels short and scannable.
rules.do: Use concise labels like "New", "Active", "Draft", "Beta", or "Past due".
rules.dont: Use long phrases or sentence-style labels inside badges.

rules.requirement: Use badges to communicate status, category, count, or metadata.
rules.do: Use badges for states like "Approved", "Pending", "Error", "Optional", or "Required".
rules.dont: Use badges for primary actions or navigational controls.

rules.requirement: Do not make badges interactive unless the interaction is explicit and necessary.
rules.do: Use a button, chip, tag, or link pattern when the element is clickable.
rules.dont: Make a badge clickable without clear affordance, focus state, or accessible role.

rules.requirement: Do not rely on color alone to communicate meaning.
rules.do: Pair color with text such as "Error", "Success", "Warning", or "Inactive".
rules.dont: Use only red, green, yellow, or gray to indicate status.

rules.requirement: Ensure badge text and icons meet contrast requirements against the badge background.
rules.do: Use color pairings that maintain readable contrast in all themes and states.
rules.dont: Use pale text on pale backgrounds or saturated combinations that reduce legibility.

rules.requirement: Use badge colors and variants consistently across the product.
rules.do: Reserve semantic variants like success, warning, error, info, and neutral for consistent meanings.
rules.dont: Use the same color to mean different things in different contexts.

rules.requirement: Prefer semantic variants over one-off custom styles.
rules.do: Use standard variants such as neutral, brand, info, success, warning, error, and inverse.
rules.dont: Create screen-specific badge colors unless the system explicitly supports them.

rules.requirement: Use icons only when they add meaning or improve recognition.
rules.do: Pair an icon with a label for statuses that benefit from quick recognition.
rules.dont: Add decorative icons that increase clutter without improving understanding.

rules.requirement: Do not require icons for badge comprehension.
rules.do: Make the text label sufficient on its own.
rules.dont: Depend on an icon as the only way to distinguish badge meaning.

rules.requirement: Use a readable text size for badge labels.
rules.do: Keep badge text large enough to read comfortably at normal interface scale.
rules.dont: Use overly small text to make badges feel compact.

rules.requirement: Use consistent badge height and vertical alignment.
rules.do: Align badges visually with adjacent text, headings, table content, or form labels.
rules.dont: Let badge height vary unpredictably across variants with similar purpose.

rules.requirement: Match badge padding and spacing to the density of the surrounding UI.
rules.do: Use compact spacing in tables and denser areas, and more comfortable spacing in cards or page headers.
rules.dont: Use oversized badges in dense content or cramped badges in prominent areas.

rules.requirement: Align inline badges with the text they support.
rules.do: Place badges close to the label, title, or item they describe.
rules.dont: Separate badges so far from their related content that the relationship becomes unclear.

rules.requirement: Format count badges consistently.
rules.do: Use predictable count formats such as "3", "12", or "99+".
rules.dont: Allow large numbers to break the badge layout or create inconsistent widths.

rules.requirement: Use badges sparingly to preserve their signal value.
rules.do: Apply badges to information that benefits from quick visual scanning.
rules.dont: Badge every item, label, or attribute on the page.

rules.requirement: Ensure badge variants work across supported themes.
rules.do: Define badge tokens for background, text, border, and icon color across light, dark, and high-contrast modes.
rules.dont: Hard-code colors that only work in one theme.

rules.requirement: Define how badges behave when content is too long.
rules.do: Prefer short controlled labels, or truncate only when the full value is available elsewhere.
rules.dont: Let long badge labels wrap awkwardly or distort nearby layout.

rules.requirement: Account for translated labels that may be longer than the source language.
rules.do: Test badge layouts with longer localized strings.
rules.dont: Assume English badge length will represent all languages.

rules.requirement: Ensure the badge meaning is understandable to assistive technology.
rules.do: Use clear text labels and add accessible context when the badge alone is ambiguous.
rules.dont: Expose unexplained visual-only labels or decorative symbols as meaningful content.

rules.requirement: Match animation duration to the physical scale of what is moving.
rules.do:
Use shorter durations (quick 100ms, fast 150ms) for small elements like icon state changes,
tooltips, and badge counts. Use normal (200ms) for mid-size elements like expanding rows or
inline menus. Use slow (300ms) or slower (500ms) for large panels, full-screen overlays,
and page-level transitions.
rules.dont:
Apply the same duration to a tiny badge toggle and a full side panel entrance. A large
panel animating at 100ms feels jerky; a small badge animating at 500ms feels broken.

rules.requirement: Elements that travel greater distances should take proportionally longer.
rules.do:
A panel sliding in from off-screen (large distance) should use slow (300ms). A row
expanding in place (small distance) should use normal (200ms) or fast (150ms).
rules.dont:
Animate an element that crosses the full viewport width in the same time as one that
shifts a few pixels. The physics feel wrong and create a jarring experience.

rules.requirement: Use enter easing for elements arriving, exit easing for elements leaving, and standard easing for elements transforming in place.
rules.do:
Use --semantic-motion-easing-enter (decelerate) when a panel, dialog, or dropdown opens.
Use --semantic-motion-easing-exit (accelerate) when it closes. Use
--semantic-motion-easing-standard for toggles, state changes, and bidirectional transforms.
rules.dont:
Apply the same easing curve to both entering and exiting motion. An element that enters
fast and leaves slowly creates spatial confusion about where it came from.

rules.requirement: Reserve expressive (springy) easing for high-intent, infrequent moments only.
rules.do:
Use --semantic-motion-easing-expressive for prominent one-time transitions — a
confirmation success state, a feature introduction, or a modal opening on first use.
rules.dont:
Apply expressive easing to every hover or focus interaction. Repeated springy motion
becomes distracting and undermines the feeling of a polished product.

rules.requirement: Every animation must serve a functional purpose — it should orient, confirm, or guide.
rules.do:
Animate to show spatial relationships (where a panel came from), confirm an action
(a checkmark animating in on save), or guide attention (highlighting a newly added item).
rules.dont:
Add animation purely for visual decoration. Animations that have no functional role
increase cognitive load and slow users down on repeated tasks.

rules.requirement: Animations must never block or delay user interaction.
rules.do:
Make interactive targets (buttons, links, inputs) immediately responsive. If an element
is animating in, it should be interactive as soon as its hit area is visible — not after
the animation completes.
rules.dont:
Disable pointer events or delay focus management until an animation finishes. Users
who click or tab quickly should not be penalized by the animation timeline.

rules.requirement: All animated behavior must respect the prefers-reduced-motion: reduce media query.
rules.do:
Use the --semantic-motion-duration-* tokens for all transitions and animations.
These tokens are automatically set to 0ms when reduced motion is active. For animations
driven by JavaScript (GSAP, Framer Motion, etc.) read the media query explicitly and
skip or replace the animation.
rules.dont:
Hardcode duration values in CSS or JS. Tokens set to 0ms collapse transitions
transparently; hardcoded values remain active even for users who have requested less motion.

rules.requirement: Do not use infinite or auto-playing animations except for explicit loading states.
rules.do:
Limit looping animations to spinners, skeleton screens, and progress indicators that
communicate an ongoing async operation. Stop them as soon as the operation completes.
rules.dont:
Animate decorative elements (background gradients, floating particles, pulsing badges)
in infinite loops. Persistent motion is distracting, drains battery on mobile devices,
and can trigger vestibular disorders.

rules.requirement: Always use --semantic-motion-duration-* and --semantic-motion-easing-* tokens. Never hardcode timing values.
rules.do: transition: background var(--semantic-motion-duration-fast) var(--semantic-motion-easing-standard);
rules.dont:
transition: background 150ms ease-in-out; — hardcoded values cannot be themed,
overridden by reduced-motion, or adjusted globally.

rules.requirement: The `.a1-page-layout__body` flex row has no gap property. The sidebar and main area are adjacent with zero space between them. Any inset spacing must come from padding applied inside the main content — not from the layout itself. This ensures sidebar backgrounds and borders extend flush to the main area without a visible seam.
do: Apply padding to the element placed inside PageLayout children.
Use a Section component or a padded wrapper as the first child of main.
dont: Do not add gap, margin, or padding-inline-start to .a1-page-layout__body.
Do not add margin to .a1-page-layout__sidebar or .a1-page-layout__main.

rules.requirement: A Section used to separate large blocks of content must have at least some block padding so content does not run into the top and bottom edges.
rules.do: Give a content-separating Section a `padding` of at least `sm` (or a responsive padding) so there is breathing room above and below its content.
rules.dont: Use `padding="none"` on a Section that holds a real block of content — the first and last children will butt against the section edges and adjacent sections.

rules.requirement: Related sections (a sequence of content rows in the same flow) should use matching padding so the page rhythm stays consistent.
rules.do: Apply the same `padding` value (and the same responsive padding object) across a related group of stacked sections.
rules.dont: Mix `padding="lg"` on one row with `padding="xs"` on the next within the same content sequence — the uneven rhythm reads as a mistake.

rules.requirement: A Section used as a page's primary (top-level) outer element should almost always set a `contentWidth` so content is held to a readable measure instead of spanning the full viewport.
rules.do: Set `contentWidth` (e.g. `lg`, `xl`, or `2xl`) on each top-level Section, and use the same value on sibling sections that should align.
rules.dont: Leave `contentWidth` off a primary Section so its content stretches edge-to-edge on wide screens.

rules.requirement: A Section with a `backgroundImage` that carries text or interactive content must guarantee WCAG AA contrast over the image — photography alone is never a reliable text background.
rules.do: Pair `backgroundImage` with a `backgroundOverlay` — `darken` plus the `inverse` prop for light text, or `lighten` for the default dark text — and raise `backgroundOverlayStrength` until contrast holds over the busiest area of the image.
rules.dont: Place headings, paragraphs, or buttons directly over an un-scrimmed background image, or rely on one lucky quiet corner of the photo for readability.

rules.requirement: Section background images are decorative only — they are invisible to assistive technology and must not carry meaning.
rules.do: Use `Figure` (with alt text) when the image is content the user needs; keep `backgroundImage` for texture, atmosphere, and hero backdrops.
rules.dont: Put an infographic, product shot, or any meaning-bearing image in `backgroundImage` where screen-reader users cannot perceive it.

rules.requirement: At desktop (≥1025px) the sidebar must be sticky — it does not scroll with the page.
rules.do: Place SideNav as a sibling to the page's main content area in a flex row. The component applies `position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100vh` automatically at lg/xl, keeping the sidebar pinned to the viewport top while the page scrolls.
rules.dont: Wrap the SideNav in a container that has `overflow: hidden` or `overflow: auto` at desktop — this breaks sticky positioning. Do not apply `position: fixed` or `position: relative` overrides that interfere with stickiness.

rules.requirement: Nav items scroll internally. The header and footer slots must remain visible at all times.
rules.do: Let the nav item list grow naturally — the `.a1-side-nav__nav` region scrolls when its content overflows. The header row and footer are outside the scroll region and always stay anchored.
rules.dont: Place the header or footer content inside the nav item list, and do not set a fixed height on the sidebar that cuts off the header or footer.

rules.requirement: At mobile and tablet (≤1024px) the sidebar is a fixed overlay that slides in from the edge. It must not be persistent.
rules.do: Control visibility with the `open` prop and close it via `onClose`. Provide a menu button in the page header to re-open it. The component renders a scrim on sm/md that dismisses the drawer on click.
rules.dont: Force the sidebar to be permanently visible at mobile widths — it will cover content and break the layout.

rules.requirement: Do not use StickyActions on the same screen as BottomDrawer. Both components occupy the bottom of the viewport and will overlap. Use one or the other: StickyActions for flow navigation (onboarding, wizards, checkout, multi-step forms), BottomDrawer for persistent app-level navigation.

Always place a ButtonContainer inside StickyActions for button groups. Do not place naked buttons or icon buttons directly inside StickyActions — the ButtonContainer handles responsive button layout, fill behaviour, and alignment.

Set contentWidth on StickyActions to match the contentWidth of the Section above it so that buttons align visually with the page content. For example, if the page uses <Section contentWidth="sm">, set <StickyActions contentWidth="sm">.

StickyActions automatically renders an invisible spacer sibling in document flow whose height matches the bar. This keeps content above the bar visible without any manual paddingBlockEnd or Spacer required from the consumer. Do not add your own bottom padding to offset the bar — the spacer handles it.
Use sentence case for headings.
rules.do: Write headings like "Create account", "Payment details", or "Recent activity".
rules.dont: Write headings in title case like "Create Account", "Payment Details", or "Recent Activity".

rules.requirement: Never change font-weight on interactive or selection states.
rules.do: Use color, border, background, or underline to communicate hover, active, focus, and selected states.
rules.dont: Apply a different font-weight on :hover, :active, :focus, [aria-selected="true"], [aria-current], or [aria-pressed] — this causes the element to resize, which can shift surrounding layout and cause reflow.

rules.requirement: Do not use uppercase transforms on content text.
rules.do: Write "Submit form" or "Recent activity" — sentence-case content reads clearly for all users.
rules.dont: Apply text-transform uppercase or write all-caps content, as screen readers may spell out individual characters.

rules.requirement: Every visual value must come from a design token — never hardcode a raw colour, spacing, font, radius, shadow, or duration.
rules.do: Reference a CSS custom property that maps to a Style Dictionary token, e.g. color of var(--semantic-color-action-background). If no token fits, add one to system/tokens/ first.
rules.dont: Write a raw hex/rgb/hsl colour (or other raw value) in a style declaration, inline style, or component CSS. A raw fallback in var(--token, …) is allowed only for a token guaranteed to exist.

rules.requirement: Place a Toolbar on a panel or page surface only — never on a raised surface.
rules.do: Use a Toolbar on the page background or a panel surface (e.g. the configurator/editor side panel), where its raised background reads clearly against the surface beneath it.
rules.dont: Place a Toolbar on a raised surface — its bar uses the raised surface token, so it would have no contrast against a raised background and the toolbar would visually disappear.

rules.requirement: Tooltip content must be short, descriptive, and non-interactive.
rules.do: Use a Tooltip for brief supporting context, such as naming an icon-only action or clarifying a disabled-looking affordance.
rules.dont: Put buttons, links, form fields, menus, lengthy instructions, or essential task content inside a Tooltip.

rules.requirement: Do not make Tooltip the only way to understand or complete a task.
rules.do: Keep visible labels, helper text, validation messages, and page instructions available without hovering.
rules.dont: Hide required instructions, error recovery, pricing, legal text, or other essential information only inside a Tooltip.

rules.requirement: Tooltip triggers must be keyboard focusable when the tooltip carries useful information.
rules.do: Wrap a focusable control such as Button, IconButton, Link, or an element with a valid interactive role and keyboard handling.
rules.dont: Attach a Tooltip to static text or decorative icons when keyboard and screen-reader users need the tooltip content.

docs.title: A1 Agent Brief
docs.description: Self-contained brief for generating A1 page/project JSON: page-definition + project-bundle shapes, the full component type registry, value vocabularies, rules, and worked examples.
docs.text:
# A1 Agent Brief — build A1 pages & projects from JSON (zero context)

This single file is everything an agent needs to **generate valid A1 page-definition JSON** (and project bundles) with no other context. It is self-contained: the JSON format, the full component list with props, the value vocabularies, the rules, and worked examples.

- The rendered page is **derived from the JSON** — the JSON is the source of truth.
- Output is rendered by the a1-web Editor (`?page=editor`) and importable via **Projects → Upload JSON**.
- When something here is ambiguous, the ground truth is the code: `apps/a1-web/src/editor/pageTypes.ts` (types), `apps/a1-web/src/editor/componentRegistry.ts` (renderable set), and `packages/react/ai/components.md` (exhaustive per-component props).

---

## 1. The two JSON shapes

### A. Page definition (one page)

```jsonc
{
  "schemaVersion": "0.1.0",
  "page": {
    "id": "home",
    "name": "Home",
    "description": "Optional.",
    "layout": {
      "type": "PageLayout",
      "props": {},
      "regions": [
        { "id": "main", "name": "Main", "nodes": [ /* ComponentNode[] */ ] }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

### B. Project bundle (a multi-page project — what "Upload JSON" accepts)

```jsonc
{
  "name": "Marketing site",
  "description": "Optional.",
  "icon": "rocket_launch",          // optional Material Symbol
  "theme": "kong",                  // optional project-scoped theme key
  "pages": [
    {
      "id": "home",                  // optional key; used only to wire parentId
      "title": "Home",
      "icon": "home",                // optional
      "description": "Optional.",
      "parentId": null,              // optional; another page's id → nests it (max depth 3)
      "definition": { /* a full page definition object, shape A above */ }
    },
    { "id": "about", "title": "About", "parentId": "home", "definition": { /* … */ } }
  ]
}
```

- The uploader also accepts a **bare page definition** (shape A) and wraps it as a one-page project.
- `definition` may be the object (preferred) or a JSON string. Omit it for a blank page.
- A page's **level** (1–3) is derived from the `parentId` chain; it auto-generates a TopHeader nav.
- `theme` applies only to this project's editor canvas and launched prototype pages. It does not change the a1-web app shell theme.

---

## 2. `ComponentNode`

One node = one A1 component instance.

```jsonc
{
  "id": "hero-title",                              // required, unique in the definition
  "type": "Heading",                                // required, exact A1 component name
  "props": { "as": "h1", "size": { "xs": "lg", "md": "xl" } },
  "utilities": { "maxWidth": "lg", "marginBlock": "24" },
  "content": { "fallback": "Build pages from JSON", "textKey": "home.hero.title" },
  "a11y": { "labelledBy": "hero-title" },
  "actions": { "onClick": { "type": "navigate", "target": "/about" } },
  "children": [ /* ComponentNode[] */ ]
}
```

| Field | Required | Notes |
|-------|:--------:|-------|
| `id` | ✓ | Unique, stable. |
| `type` | ✓ | Exact PascalCase A1 name from the registry (§4). Unknown → safe visible fallback. |
| `props` | — | Forwarded verbatim to the component — **must be real props** (§4/§5). |
| `utilities` | — | Tokenized utility selections, validated by component type. Current keys: `padding`, `paddingBlock`, `paddingInline`, `margin`, `marginBlock`, `marginInline`, `gap`, `maxWidth`, `minWidth`. Use this instead of raw `className` for utility classes; e.g. `IconButton` rejects min/max width but `Button` can accept it. |
| `content` | — | Primary text: `{ fallback (required), textKey? }`. Resolved via labels; `fallback` always shown if no label. |
| `a11y` | — | `{ label→aria-label, labelledBy→aria-labelledby, describedBy→aria-describedby, role }`. |
| `actions` | — | Declared, **not executed yet** (`navigate`/`openDialog`/`appAction`/`submitForm`/`externalLink` + `target`). Keep shape stable. |
| `children` | — | Nested nodes; rendered after `content`. Only meaningful on container types (§4). |

A few components take their text via a **named prop**, not `content`: **Fieldset** uses `props.legend`. Everything else uses `content.fallback`.

---

## 3. Rules (non-negotiable)

1. **A1 components only.** Every `type` is a registered A1 component. Never use HTML tags (`div`, `p`, `span`) as a `type`.
2. **Exact names.** `type` matches the exported component name exactly (PascalCase): `Heading`, `MessageBadge`, `TextField`. Don't lowercase/alias.
3. **Real props only.** Unknown prop keys leak to the DOM and warn. Use the props in §4/§5.
4. **Utilities use `utilities`, not fake props.** One-off tokenized width/spacing adjustments go in `utilities`; do not emit raw `className` utility strings unless you are preserving an existing class.
5. **Tokens, not raw values.** Use the scale values (`gap: "md"`, `size: "lg"`, `color: "muted"`) — never raw px/hex/rem in props. There is no `style` escape hatch in the definition.
6. **Semantic structure.** A heading is a `Heading`, an action is a `Button`, navigation is a `Link`. Pick the component by meaning, not looks.
7. **Never uppercase.** Author text in sentence case ("Create account"). Never ALL-CAPS content.
8. **Layout via layout components.** Use `Section`/`Stack`/`Grid`/`Card`, not ad-hoc wrappers. Put width/padding/gap on `Section` (see §5).
9. **Accessibility.** Icon-only buttons need `props["aria-label"]` (or `a11y.label`). Label form regions; don't rely on color alone.
10. **One primary action per area.** Only one `Button variant="primary"` per form/dialog/group.

### Consistency rules (projects & layout) — these keep generated pages coherent

11. **No per-page nav in a project.** A **project bundle** auto-generates the `TopHeader` from the page hierarchy. **Do not** add a `TopHeader` node to a project's pages — it duplicates the generated header. (A single standalone page may include one.)
12. **Section padding is consistent and non-zero.** Every primary (top-level) `Section` should have **non-zero `padding`** (don't leave it off or `none`), and **neighboring top-level sections should use the same `padding`** so the page has an even rhythm. Vary `surface`/`gap` for contrast, not padding.
12. **Primary sections set a `contentWidth`.** A `Section` used as a page's outer element should almost always set `contentWidth` (e.g. `lg`/`xl`/`2xl`) so content doesn't span the full viewport. Use the same `contentWidth` for sibling sections that should align.
13. **Cards live in a Grid.** Two or more sibling `Card`s should be wrapped in a `Grid` (e.g. `columns: { xs: 1, md: 3 }`), not loose in a `Stack`/`Section`.
14. **Card images use a valid, consistent `aspectRatio`.** A `Figure` inside a `Card` should set `aspectRatio` to one of the **token values** — `"16:9" "4:3" "3:2" "1:1" "2:3" "3:4" "9:16" "21:9"` (note the colon, **not** `"4 / 3"`) — and all cards in a grid should use the **same** ratio.

---

## 4. Component registry — type · container · role · key props

`C` = container (accepts `children`). Sizes/values are defined in §5. Props listed are the common ones; see `components.md` for the full set.

### Layout & display
| type | C | role | key props |
|------|:-:|------|-----------|
| `PageLayout` | C | App-shell layout (top of `page.layout`). **Does not** take width/padding/gap — put those on `Section`. | (slots managed by layout) |
| `Section` | C | Page region: surface, padding, width, gap, border, alignment, background image. | `padding` (none–xl), `gap` (xs–xxl), `contentWidth` (xs–2xl), `surface` (page/panel/raised), `align` (none/start/center/end), `inverse` (bool), `gradient`, `height` (auto/screen/hero), `as`, `borderSize`/`borderStyle`/`borderVariant`/`borderSides`, `radius`, `backgroundImage` (URL, decorative; suppresses `gradient`), `backgroundFit` (cover/contain/tile), `backgroundPosition` (9 focal points), `backgroundOverlay` (darken/lighten — always add one under text; pair darken with `inverse`), `backgroundOverlayStrength` (sm/md/lg) |
| `Stack` | C | Linear layout. | `direction` (column/row, responsive), `gap` (xs–xxl), `align`, `justify`, `wrap` (bool), `as` |
| `Grid` | C | Multi-column grid. | `columns` (number or `{xs,md,…}`), `gap`, `rowGap`, `columnGap` |
| `GridItem` | C | Direct child of `Grid` for column/row spanning. | `span` (number/`full`/responsive), `rowSpan` (number/responsive) |
| `Cluster` | C | Wrapping row of items (deprecated — prefer `Stack direction="row" wrap`). | `gap`, `align`, `justify` |
| `Card` | C | Bounded, repeatable content unit. | `variant` (default/navigation), `href` (navigation), `icon`, `heroIcon`, `iconDisplay` |
| `Bleed` | C | Reach past surrounding inset padding. | `space` (spacing number) |
| `Inset` | C | Uniform padding around content. | `space` (spacing number) |
| `Spacer` | — | Fixed gap. | `size` (xs–xxl) |
| `ButtonContainer` | C | Responsive row of action buttons. | `align` (start/center/end), `fillButtons` (bool) |
| `Slot` | C | Constrained "blank area" (pattern authoring). | `label`, `allow` (type[]), `allowPatterns` (id[]), `min`, `max`, `columns`, `gap` |
| `Outlet` | C | Shared project-layout insertion point for page content. | `name` |
| `Divider` | — | Visual separator. | `orientation`, `variant` (subtle/strong/accent), `lineStyle` (solid/dashed/dotted), `size`, `space` |
| `Figure` | — | Image with optional caption. | `src` (req), `alt`, `caption`, `radius`, `size` (3xs–xxl), `align`, `aspectRatio` (**colon form**: `16:9`/`4:3`/`3:2`/`1:1`/`2:3`/`3:4`/`9:16`/`21:9`), `crop` |
| `Icon` | — | Material Symbol. | `name` (req — see §5 icons), `size` (xs–xl/jumbo), `color`, `fill` (bool) |

### Typography (text via `content.fallback`)
| type | C | role | key props |
|------|:-:|------|-----------|
| `Heading` | — | Heading. | `as` (h1–h6/p/span), `type` (heading/display), `size` (xs–xxl; display adds jumbo/xJumbo), `color`, `align` |
| `Paragraph` | — | Body text. | `size` (xs–xl), `color` (default/muted/…), `align` |
| `Blockquote` | — | Quotation. | `variant` (border/feature), `cite` |
| `Code` | — | Code. | `variant` (inline/block), `wrapping` (bool), `copyCode` (bool) |
| `List` | C | List (children are `ListItem`). | `as` (ul/ol), `variant` (unordered/ordered/icon), `size`, `icon` (icon variant) |
| `ListItem` | — | List item (only inside `List`). | `icon` |

### Actions & controls
| type | C | role | key props |
|------|:-:|------|-----------|
| `Button` | — | Action. | `variant` (primary/secondary/tertiary/destructive/success), `size` (sm/md/lg), `icon`, `iconPosition` (start/end), `fullWidth` (bool), `loading` (bool), `disabled` (bool), `as` (button/a) + `href` |
| `Link` | — | Navigation. text via `content`. | `href`, `external` (bool), `size` |
| `IconButton` | — | Icon-only action. **needs `aria-label`.** | `icon` (req), `aria-label` (req), `variant`, `size` (sm/md/lg), `as`/`href` |
| `Switch` | — | On/off toggle. | `label`, `checked` (bool), `size` |
| `SegmentedControl` | — | Compact single-select. | `options` (`{value,label}[]`), `value`, `size` |
| `Slider` | — | Range / detent slider. | `label`, `value`, `min`, `max`, `step`, `detents`, `size`, `variant` |
| `Toolbar` | C | Compact control bar. | `label`, `aria-label`, `overlay`, `fullWidth` |
| `Tabs` | C | Tabbed nav / stepper. | `variant` (line/pills/segment/progress/folder), `value`; panel content goes on matching `items[].children` |
| `Accordion` | C | Disclosure. | `label`, `subtext`, `divider` (bool), `defaultOpen` (bool), `size` |
| `StickyActions` | C | Fixed bottom action bar (nest a `ButtonContainer`). | `contentWidth` |

### Inputs (label via `props.label`; no `placeholder` by design)
| type | C | role | key props |
|------|:-:|------|-----------|
| `TextField` | — | Text/email/password. | `label`, `type` (text/email/password), `value`, `hint`, `error`, `success`, `required`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `size` (compact/default/comfortable), `labelPosition` (above/before), `autoComplete` |
| `TextareaField` | — | Multiline. | `label`, `value`, `rows`, + field-family props |
| `SelectField` | — | Select. | `label`, `options` (`{value,label}[]`), `value`; Figma preview uses `showValue: true` + `defaultValue`, + field-family props |
| `NumberField` | — | Number. | `label`, `prefix`, `unit`, + field-family props |
| `DateField` `TimeField` `PhoneField` `ZipField` `CreditCardField` | — | Masked fields. | `label`, `value`, + field-family props |
| `Fieldset` | C | Group of fields. **legend via `props.legend`.** | `legend`, `labelPosition` |
| `FieldRow` | C | Lay out fields in equal columns. | (children only) |
| `CheckboxGroup` `RadioGroup` | — | Multi/single choice. | `label`, `options` (`{value,label}[]`), `value`, `columns`, `size` |
| `ChoiceGroup` | — | Tile selector. | `options`/`sections`, `value`, `multiple` (bool), `columns`, `size`, `inlineIcon` |

### Feedback & messaging
| type | C | role | key props |
|------|:-:|------|-----------|
| `Banner` | C | In-page / system alert. | `status` (neutral/info/success/warn/error), `variant` (inline/system), `title`, `icon`, `onDismiss` |
| `MessageBadge` | — | Status/label badge. text via `content`. | `status` (neutral/info/success/warn/error), `subtle` (bool), `size`, `icon` |
| `MessageEmptyState` | — | Empty state. | `scale` (page/section/card), `icon`, `title`, `description`, `action` |
| `StatusBar` | — | Progress bar. | `value`, `max`, `size`, `label`, `labelPosition`, `indeterminate` |
| `CircularProgress` | — | Ring progress. | `value`, `max`, `size`, `indeterminate`, `aria-label` |
| `StepTracker` | — | Step position indicator. | `steps`, `current`, `align` |

### Navigation & data
| type | C | role | key props |
|------|:-:|------|-----------|
| `Breadcrumb` | — | Breadcrumb trail. | `items` (`{label,href?}[]`) |
| `TopHeader` | — | Top nav bar. | `logo`, `navItems`, `navIconPosition` |
| `BottomDrawer` | — | Bottom nav (≤5). | `items` (`{id,label,icon,href?}[]`), `aria-label` (req) |
| `PageNav` | — | In-page section nav. | `label`, `sections` (`{id,label,level}[]`) |
| `TreeMenu` | — | Hierarchical tree. | `items`, `variant` (`expanded`/`collapsed`), `selectedId`, `showExpandControls` |
| `Pagination` | — | Pager. | `page`, `pageCount`, `onPageChange` |
| `DefinitionList` | — | Label/value pairs. | `items` (`{label,value}[]`; `label` is required and renders the term; do not use `term`), `direction` (row/column), `size`, `labelWidth` |
| `DataTable` | — | Table. | `columns` (`{key,label}[]`), `rows` (objects keyed by each column `key`, include a unique `id`), `size` (**`comfortable`/`default`/`compact`** — not sm/md/lg; omit for auto), `notices` |
| `Calendar` | — | Calendar (experimental). | `variant`, `initialMonth`, `selectable` |

> **Note:** `TopHeader`, `BottomDrawer`, `PageNav`, `TreeMenu`, `DataTable`, `Tabs`, `Toolbar`, `Slider`, `Calendar`, `Pagination` take structured array/object props — generate them sparingly and follow the prop shapes in `components.md` if used.

---

## 5. Shared value vocabularies

- **Spacing / gap** (`gap`, `padding`, `space`, `Spacer.size`): `none`, `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, `xxl`. (Numeric spacing for `Inset`/`Bleed`/`Divider.space`: `4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64`.)
- **Section `contentWidth`**: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, `2xl`.
- **Heading/Figure `size`**: `xs, sm, md, lg, xl, xxl` (Heading `type="display"` adds `jumbo`, `xJumbo`; Figure adds `3xs, 2xs, …`). Paragraph `size`: `xs–xl`.
- **Field-family `size`**: `compact`, `default`, `comfortable`. Most other components: `sm`, `md`, `lg`.
- **`color`** (text/icon): `default`, `muted`, `accent`, `inverse`, `success`, `error`, `warn`, `info`.
- **`status`** (Banner/MessageBadge/etc.): `neutral`, `info`, `success`, `warn`, `error`.
- **Section `surface`**: `page`, `panel`, `raised`, `card`. **`align`**: `none`, `start`, `center`, `end`.
- **Section background image**: `backgroundFit`: `cover` (default), `contain`, `tile`. `backgroundPosition`: `center` (default), `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`, `top-left`, `top-right`, `bottom-left`, `bottom-right`. `backgroundOverlay`: `darken`, `lighten` (`backgroundOverlayStrength`: `sm`, `md` default, `lg`). A section with text over a `backgroundImage` must set a `backgroundOverlay` — `darken` + `inverse: true` for light text, `lighten` for dark text.
- **Button `variant`**: `primary`, `secondary`, `tertiary`, `destructive`, `success`. **`size`**: `sm`, `md`, `lg`.
- **Responsive**: any prop may take a breakpoint object using `xs, sm, md, lg, xl`, e.g. `"columns": { "xs": 1, "md": 3 }`, `"direction": { "xs": "column", "md": "row" }`.
- **Icons** (`Icon.name`, `*.icon`): use Material Symbols Outlined names (snake_case), e.g. `home`, `add`, `search`, `settings`, `arrow_forward`, `check_circle`, `download`, `rocket_launch`. Project definitions may also use `custom:<snake_case_name>` when that custom icon is registered for the project.

---

## 6. Worked examples

### Single page (hero + a 2-up card row)
```jsonc
{
  "schemaVersion": "0.1.0",
  "page": {
    "id": "home", "name": "Home",
    "layout": { "type": "PageLayout", "regions": [ { "id": "main", "nodes": [
      { "id": "hero", "type": "Section",
        "props": { "padding": "xl", "contentWidth": "lg", "gap": "md", "align": "center" },
        "children": [
          { "id": "hero-eyebrow", "type": "Paragraph", "props": { "size": "sm", "color": "muted" }, "content": { "fallback": "A1 Design System" } },
          { "id": "hero-title", "type": "Heading", "props": { "as": "h1", "type": "display", "size": { "xs": "lg", "md": "xl" } }, "content": { "fallback": "Build pages from structured JSON" } },
          { "id": "hero-body", "type": "Paragraph", "props": { "size": "lg", "color": "muted" }, "content": { "fallback": "Describe the page as data; A1 renders the components." } },
          { "id": "hero-cta", "type": "ButtonContainer", "props": { "align": "center" },
            "children": [
              { "id": "hero-primary", "type": "Button", "props": { "variant": "primary", "icon": "rocket_launch" }, "content": { "fallback": "Get started" } },
              { "id": "hero-secondary", "type": "Button", "props": { "variant": "secondary" }, "content": { "fallback": "Learn more" } }
            ] }
        ] },
      { "id": "features", "type": "Section", "props": { "padding": "xl", "contentWidth": "lg", "gap": "lg" },
        "children": [
          { "id": "features-title", "type": "Heading", "props": { "as": "h2", "size": "lg", "align": "center" }, "content": { "fallback": "Built for teams" } },
          { "id": "features-grid", "type": "Grid", "props": { "columns": { "xs": 1, "md": 2 }, "gap": "md" },
            "children": [
              { "id": "card-1", "type": "Card", "props": { "icon": "bolt" }, "children": [
                { "id": "card-1-h", "type": "Heading", "props": { "as": "h3", "size": "sm" }, "content": { "fallback": "Fast by default" } },
                { "id": "card-1-p", "type": "Paragraph", "props": { "size": "sm", "color": "muted" }, "content": { "fallback": "Performant out of the box." } }
              ] },
              { "id": "card-2", "type": "Card", "props": { "icon": "shield" }, "children": [
                { "id": "card-2-h", "type": "Heading", "props": { "as": "h3", "size": "sm" }, "content": { "fallback": "Accessible" } },
                { "id": "card-2-p", "type": "Paragraph", "props": { "size": "sm", "color": "muted" }, "content": { "fallback": "WCAG-minded components." } }
              ] }
            ] }
        ] }
    ] } ] }
  }
}
```

### Project bundle (paste into Projects → Upload JSON)
```jsonc
{
  "name": "Starter site", "icon": "rocket_launch",
  "pages": [
    { "id": "home", "title": "Home", "icon": "home", "definition": { /* a page definition like above */ } },
    { "id": "about", "title": "About", "parentId": "home", "definition": {
      "schemaVersion": "0.1.0",
      "page": { "id": "about", "name": "About", "layout": { "type": "PageLayout", "regions": [ { "id": "main", "nodes": [
        { "id": "s", "type": "Section", "props": { "padding": "xl", "contentWidth": "md", "gap": "md" }, "children": [
          { "id": "h", "type": "Heading", "props": { "as": "h1", "size": "xl" }, "content": { "fallback": "About us" } },
          { "id": "p", "type": "Paragraph", "content": { "fallback": "A nested page (level 2 under Home)." } }
        ] }
      ] } ] } }
    } }
  ]
}
```

---

## 7. Do / Don't

- **Do** give every node a unique `id`; put all text in `content.fallback`; put width/padding/gap on `Section`, not `PageLayout`.
- **Do** use responsive objects for breakpoint changes; use only registry component names; use scale values for every prop.
- **Don't** use HTML tag names as `type`; pass props a component doesn't have; raw px/hex/rem in props; ALL-CAPS text; icon-only `IconButton` without `aria-label`.
- **Don't** nest a `Section` inside another layout to constrain it; don't nest `Card` in `Card`; don't put interactive controls inside a `Card variant="navigation"`.

> Unknown component types and unknown props won't crash — unknown `type` renders a labeled fallback. But both are bugs to fix, not features.
